claims.text: A thin Cu coating on FeMnNiGeSi-type microribbons creates controlled interfacial strain.
The coating-induced interfacial strain modifies nucleation dynamics of the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Modified nucleation dynamics broaden the magnetostructural transition.
Modified nucleation dynamics reduce transition hysteresis.
A Cu coating enhances heat exchange in the coated alloy.
Annealing near 200°C activates interfacial strain without altering the alloy's intrinsic microstructure.
The Cu coating produces uniform interfacial strain.
Interfacial strain lowers local energy barriers for the magnetostructural transition.
Lower local transition barriers smooth and broaden the transition.
Smoothing and broadening the transition reduces hysteresis.
Copper's high thermal conductivity improves heat exchange during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Cu-coated microribbons will retain a competitive magnetocaloric entropy change relative to the uncoated baseline.
As-deposited, uncoated melt-spun microribbons exhibit a sharp, hysteretic magnetostructural transition.
As-deposited, uncoated melt-spun microribbons have limited heat-exchange performance.

The predicted effects apply to rare-earth-free, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type microribbons or thin films under low-applied-field cooling cycles when coated with approximately 50 nm of Cu and mildly annealed.

contradictions.description: The mechanism asserts that the coating induces uniform interfacial strain, whereas the uncertainty field anticipates variations in strain distribution due to adhesion. Uniformity is therefore asserted more strongly than the stated uncertainty permits.
